speaker: Chris
en:
The Volkswagen Type 1 is one little car that made
a big splash in automotive history.
Designed as a functional civilian car by none other than
Ferdinand Porsche…

...its distinctive rounded shape resulted in the nickname,
"Beetle." 
Its production run spanned more than 60 years, producing
21,529,464 units from the 1940s to the early 2000s.

Thus, the Type 1 is considered one of the most historically
significant cars ever.

speaker: Jeremy
en:
�sseq scmd="GTCafe_Conv_Standard01">This second-generation NSX-GT race car appeared in 2014.

Does that sound odd to you?
It should, because the second-generation NSX production
car was released two years later in 2016.
There's simple explanation to this.

The race NSX wasn't based on the production NSX, but on
the NSX Concept...
...which was unveiled ahead of the production version
in 2014.

�And, it was this concept car that took
the GT name.
In mid-2016, the second-generation NSX production car
was officially released.

Because of this, the competition car was also called
the NSX-GT.
This car came in 3rd place in Round Five of the
Super GT in Japan.�

speaker: Stella
en:
Oh, I’ve seen this car before in a "Fast & Furious" film.
It’s the Toyota Supra.
As the ancestor of the GR Supra, it has a special
place in Toyota’s sports-car history.
And there’s something really neat about
its emblem, too.

It was actually inspired by the art of
Japanese calligraphy.|

speaker: Hideo Kodama
en:
Classical yet elegantly refined, 
this car is truly a stunning work of art.

Carrozzeria Touring, were experimenting with an 
advanced design called the "pontoon,"

where the front and rear fenders were connected.
However, this 8C 2900 has...

...a classic design where 
the large fenders are enhanced.
Of course, other Alfa Romeos had this design element.

Undoubtedly a very beautiful car that caught people's 
eye even more so than Ferraris of today.

speaker: Hideo Kodama
en:
This is one of Toyota’s best designs in recent years.

It's been over a decade since this car
hit the streets.

Yet to see it today, you’d think it were novel.
The low height and its double-bubble roof result in a drag
coefficient of 0.28, allowing for a smooth ride.

From the significantly canted windscreen...

...to the drastically sloping rear, this car expresses
a bold, clear vision.!

speaker: Fabio Filippini
en:
�sseq scmd="GTCafe_Conv_Standard01">The Ferrari Enzo, named after Ferrari’s founder, marked
a radical stylistic change in Ferrari’s history.

It was certainly one of the most iconic sports cars of the 2000s.
Directly inspired by the aerodynamic shapes
of contemporary Formula 1 machines...

...it made a lasting impression with its pointed nose.
Like a jetfighter, driven by functionality and performance, 
its intersecting blocks�created space for its air intakes.

The cabin was also clearly inspired by aeronautical shapes.
At the rear, there appeared, for the first time, 
dual circular taillights...

...which would later be found on the F430
and other subsequent Ferraris.*

speaker: Ed Welburn
en:
The Lexus LC 500 has absolutely incredible proportions.
With a long, low hood, a long wheelbase...
...a tight cabin, large wheels placed 
at the corners...

...and an absolutely juicy body shape,
which is well-sculpted.
 
It has very technical headlamps and taillamps,
and a fresh interpretation of the Lexus grille.
This design makes it very clear that a highly advanced
engine is under the hood. I absolutely love this car!

speaker: Freeman Thomas
en:
The Raptor is an aggressive and capable beast.
I love this truck!
It has a solid overall design and possesses plenty of Ford’s
unique DNA.

The wide stance and large tires result in great
handling character and tremendous height.

Its capable 4WD system allows it to excel
on rough off-road terrain.
This first-generation Raptor had a V-8 that matched 
its aggressive character.=

speaker: Jeremy
en:
In 2022, scarcely a year after its first appearance...

...the ELANTRA N TC rose to the top, claiming the crown 
at the very pinnacle of global TCR competition.
Even now, it continues to assert its authority as
a constant force on the world stage.
And who could overlook its astonishing performance
at the Nürburgring 24h in May 2025?

That was the moment the ELANTRA N TC delivered an improbable
1–2 finish in the TCR Class!
Remarkably, it also marked Hyundai’s fifth straight class victory
at this legendary endurance race.

speaker: Jeremy
en:
Beginning in 1966, the first-generation Ford GT
claimed four consecutive wins at Le Mans.
Thirty-six years later, in 2005, a reproduction model
was released to celebrate Ford’s centennial.

About 1,500 units of this reproduction model
were sold as road cars.
But what if this car were to race at Le Mans today?
Developed for Gran Turismo, this Ford GT LM Race Car
Spec II tries to answer that question.

Just wait until you see its speed on the straights!?

speaker: Hideo Kodama
en:
A company that’s known to pivot hard, Suzuki sometimes
offers products that really take you by surprise.

The Wagon R was one such example. And so
 was this Swift Sport.
The four corners of its chunky body are fit with relatively
large wheels that speak to its excellent maneuverability.

A small car, it’s equipped with everything it needs
and nothing else.
If you were to see it driving down an Italian street, you’d 
think the car was designed by Italians.

speaker: Hikonori Kagurazaka
en:
�sseq scmd="GTCafe_Conv_Standard01">One of the roles design plays in industrial products is...

...to instantly convey information and the underlying message 
in a visual way that may not be noticed at first glance.

It is to project the functional excellence of the product, its
philosophy, tradition and the creator's intent, instantly.

It's also supposed to draw the customer in 
by eliciting a "love at first sight" appeal. 
Therefore, the look of products at time� tries to appeal to
many people at once, making many of them looking similar.

Bluntly put, design is usually dictated by the market.
But in the case of the Radical, this is not the case.

Whether it's a mountain road or the race track,
all it needs to do is to go fast.
The headlight, for example, is simply required
to shine a light forward. 
Although seemingly unapproachable, this car kno�s its role.
It’s a one-of-a-kind sidekick that requires a special love.

These types of cars make life entertaining, don't you think?i

speaker: Fabio Filippini
en:
This is the high-performance version of the F430, developed
with the help of Michael Schumacher.
Stylistically, it is distinguished by a sharp front, large
air intakes, and enhanced brake cooling ducts.
However, the biggest difference is in the rear.

Here we have a large engine grille...

...and a big diffuser framed by a band with two large, round
exhausts on either side of the license plate.
To emphasize its sportiness, the side mirrors have been done
in carbon fiber...
And a two-tone livery is available as an option.

speaker: Stella
en:
The Honda Fit is one of Japan's most popular compact cars.
By the time this third-generation model made its debut in 2013,
2,000,000 units had been sold in Japan alone!

It is a perennial bestseller.
From this model on, the Fit Hybrid began featuring
a more powerful engine.
Which reminds me, have you heard of the Civic?
It's another Honda compact car.
Like the Fit, the Civic is a front-wheel-drive
compact.

And it drives just like a sports car!p

speaker: Tom Matano
en:
This is a genuine American muscle car that cuts
a distinctive figure on the track.
A mid-size sedan with a super-high horsepower engine...

...it’s more European in its aero parts and suspension
than the first-gen model.
This car is a celebration of American "inclusive design."

It offers supercar-level performance
at an affordable price.
I once drove a Chrysler 300 SRT at Laguna Seca Raceway.

A dream to drive, its wide torque range allowed me to take
the course without frequent gear shifts.

speaker: Hideo Kodama
en:
There seems to be a reason behind every detail of this design,
a design with the spirit of rationality.

Yet it possesses irresistible charm.
This is the W194, also known as the 300SL.
It won the Mille Miglia, Grand Prix of Bern, 
and the Carrera Panamericana in 1952.

On top of that, it placed 1-2 at Le Mans.
The doors of this car swing upward in 
what is known as "gullwing" types. 

That term also serves as the nickname for this car. 

This design is the result of avoiding the bottom portion
 of the structure of the space frame./

speaker: Ed Welburn
en:
The GT Concept Car by Citroën has a very intriguing design.

Its center fuselage disappears behind
its very bold fender shapes.
This gives the car a sleek and aggressive look and helps
to manage air flow and cooling in a unique way.
The windshield and side glass are like slits, giving the
GT by Citroën a very private, sinister look.

speaker: Freeman Thomas
en:

speaker: Kunihisa Ito
en:
Designed and built by Chrysler's Advanced Design Studios
over the course of 1988 and 1989...

...the Viper was dubbed the "second-coming"
of the Shelby Cobra.

It was co-produced by then-president Bob Lutz
and designer Tom Gale.
Heralding a new era at the New York Auto Show in 2012,
the SRT GTS-R marked the series’ return to racing.
Distinguished by a long nose and short deck body...
...its flat bottom and wing addition dramatically
improved aerodynamics.

speaker: Stella
en:
Oh great! It's a car that runs on two power sources: 
a gasoline engine and an electric motor.

Electric motors are great for accelerating, 
and they don't burn fuel.
By balancing engine and motor power, hybrid cars offer
a very efficient driving experience.

speaker: Stella
en:
I thought this was a FIAT 500 at first,
but this car's called an Abarth? 

It's still just as cute,
and the engine sounds amazing!
The Scorpion emblem adds a touch of class as well.

It traces back to the company's founder who was born
under the Scorpio zodiac sign. That's really cool!

speaker: Fabio Filippini
en:
The plexiglass headlights on the early models and...

...design elements such as the orange indicator lights that
extend on the side...

...are defining symbols of this car.
Also, the grooves that flow in a straight line on the side
of the car are...

...implemented on most Ferraris that followed this car. 

The star-shaped 5-spoke aluminum wheels are also important
symbols of Ferrari's design.
Yes, yes. This wheel originated from a sports prototype car
from the 1960s...

...and was first used on the Daytona.

speaker: Chris
en:
Ford's F-Series is the most popular line of pickup trucks
in North America.

And the Raptor is by far the highest performance model
of the bunch.
One design objective was to optimize it for off-road racing,
therefore, the truck possesses sports-car-like handling.
The Raptor boasts a wide body, reinforced suspension and a 
6.2-liter V-8 capable of producing more than 400ps.
Put this beast in its element, and it'll shatter your notion
of how fast a truck can go.

speaker: Jeremy
en:

speaker: Chris
en:
This is a first-generation Honda Civic Type R.
What's really special about this car is its specially tuned
naturally-aspirated 1.6-liter inline-4.
Just wait till you hear its thrilling roar and exhaust note.
You'll think you're driving a genuine race car!

It really comes on in the upper ranges, especially when
you rev the engine to 8000rpm.
Since it's a front-wheel-drive car, the Type R was
originally available with an affordable price tag.

But nowadays its value has been reassessed
owing to its exceptional performance.

speaker: Tom Matano
en:
An iconic creamy white body with the Shelby Blue stripes 
represented a genuine GT Mustang...

...one that stood out from the super popular base model.
The original Mustang came 
with great proportions. 

Its design was simple and clean.

Due to regulations, no parts 
were added to the exterior of the Shelby G.T.350.
However, it did come with a lowered suspension, 
wider tires and the iconic graphics.

 If I were to own a Mustang, 
this would be at the top of my list.

speaker: Sarah
en:
That's correct! It's an engine created by Porsche's
legendary engineer Hans Mezger!

He's responsible for the 911's traditional air-cooled
engines, as well as race engines for F1 and Le Mans.

Although 911 engines became water-cooled starting with
the 996...

...the engines for the GT2, GT3 and Turbo
were still rooted in designs by Mezger.

speaker: Freeman Thomas
en:
The 2016 TT Cup is exciting in that it's 
an extremely well-proportioned racecar...

...when compared to the production-based street version. 

I like the fender forms that hint at the original TT, 
but these are bolder and wider.
The graphics are pure Audi Sport 
with the red, gray and silver.

I also like the black wheels brought out 
to the maximum track width.
It gives the car an amazing stance that's more absolute!

speaker: Ikuo Maeda
en:
�sseq scmd="GTCafe_Conv_Standard01">The RX-VISION is a car in which I placed
my car designer life on the line.

I worked on it from the standpoint of really making 
the dream sports car I have in my mind.
And one of the most important things for a sports car 
is its fundamental structure.

Historic cars that are still popular and beautiful to look at
today all have exceptionally great proportions.

So the first thing we worked on for the RX-VISION 
was also the s�ructure.
A textbook FR (Front Engine Rear Drive) with a long nose, 
and the ability to place proper load on the rear wheels.

In the final stages, we extended the front nose about 150mm 
from the structure we had originally designed,

the part from the front doors up to the front wheel center.
In the very end we made it a slightly unbalanced proportion...

But at that moment we got a lot of traction on the rear wheels,
and�thought "This will work!"

That slight unbalance is the hook. It's the secret
to making someone go "Hmm".
The other secret is the reflection of light.

If you look at the RX-VISION as you circle it, I think you'll
notice that the light's reflection moves around like a creature.
Cars are like family or friends to those who are into them.

And it's a very rare industrial product 
that runs around on its own.
That makes cars have the same type of existence as animals running
around in the wild, or an athlete running on a field.

And when you think of it that way, I also want cars to be
something that looks beautiful and truly alive in nature.

And for that you need a "sense of life."
So when thinking about what is the sense of life, 
that will put cars at one with nature,

we tried to express life in the car with the light's reflections
6nd their beauty on the car's body.

And those are the type of shapes 
that are instilled in the RX-VISION.�

speaker: Ikuo Maeda
en:
I think the MAZDA3 is one of the top 5 cars
in my career as a car designer.

The design of the MAZDA3 also trails back to the RX-VISION.
In the RX-VISION, I created a form that expresses
a sense of life in the beauty of its reflections.
And the design of the MAZDA3 is an achievement of that form
created in the RX-VISION, in the C segment.
It's one of my personal favorites, and I think its a car
that will mark its name in history.

speaker: Jeremy
en:
This Audi takes me back to the 2011 Le Mans 24-hour race. 

Incredibly, it crossed the finish line and won
the competition...

A nail-biting 13.845 seconds before
the second-place Peugeot.

Rarely has Le Mans had such a close race!
Although Audi bested Peugeot in terms of speed,
the same couldn't be said about fuel efficiency.

Peugeot tried to use this to their advantage
by taking as few pitstops as possible.

So while Audi was making excellent time,
it couldn’t quite shake Peugeot.
But in the end, Audi’s speed won out, eking out
a victory against its competitor.

speaker: Hideo Kodama
en:
Following a trend set by the 4CV, the Renault R8 represented the
third generation of the marque’s rear-engine sedans.

Yet the addition of 4-wheel disc brakes made it
uniquely modern.
The R8 Gordini is an upgraded version, complete with
the magic touch of the great Amédée Gordini.

Affectionately called the "Lunchbox," it has blunt lines
and an overall spartan design.
The year 1966 saw the addition of twin headlights.

Dressed in French racing blue, with two white stripes,
the Gordini truly has a charm that differentiates it from the pack.

speaker: Jeremy
en:
The Tour de Corse?

It's a famous rally event that takes place on the
French island of Corsica.
The 1964 Tour de Corse was particularly a classic.

Only eight cars out of 79 managed to complete the race!
What's more, Renault's R8 Gordini claimed 1st, 3rd,
4th and 5th place!

It was quite the remarkable achievement.
Gordini was an engine manufacturer, originally established
by the Italian driver and engineer Amedeo Gordini.

The R8 Gordini came about through a collaboration with
Renault.

speaker: Jeremy
en:
�sseq scmd="GTCafe_Conv_CarDetail_Front">Toyota introduced this Lexus SC430 as the successor to...

The 80 Supra for the Super GT racing series.
The 2008 series in which it debuted was a heated contest
right down to the last race!

But when the Petronas Tom’s car crossed the finish line
and took the team title...

It established itself as a champion car
for the history books.
By the way, did you know that the base SC430
�was a vario-roof convertible?

To get it battle-ready, Toyota built a reinforced roof
that combined a roll cage and carbon panels...

and fit it over the original.
In other words, the SC430 GT500 is in fact
built upon a coupe body!j

speaker: Chris
en:
The Alfa Romeo 4C is a car with plenty of charm.
First and foremost, it's impressively light, 
weighing a mere 895kg!

This is rather astounding when one considers the design
trends of the 2010s.
Its innovative carbon-fiber body really
paid off in this respect.
Although powered by a small turbocharged 1.8-liter engine, the 
car's lightweight nature made it accelerate like a super car.
Moreover, its mid-engine sports car proportions 
made it a sight to behold.

It even pays homage to Alfa Romeo's historic 
Tipo 33 Stradale.

speaker: Fabio Filippini
en:
�sseq scmd="GTCafe_Conv_CarDetail_Front">A legend among supercars of the 1980s,
the Ferrari GTO...

...combined the most advanced performance, technology
and style of its era.
Despite the nominal nod to the iconic 250 GTO from 1962...

...this car actually incorporated the design of the popular 308 GTB,
though slightly stretched to match its longer wheelbase.
Its main character came from the big front-spoiler
and four rectangu�ar daylights...

...as well as the wide fenders covering its big wheels.
The gearbox hanging below the bumper
was framed by four round exhausts.

It was always a wonderful sight to see.

The only details recalling the vintage GTO...

...were the famous three slanted side vents behind the rear wheel,
and the enlarged "duck-tail" spoiler.�

speaker: Ed Welburn
en:
The Peugeot RCZ GT is a very creative design,
with styling much like a show car.

It’s sporty, youthful, and elegant in its execution.
The silver arched roofline-rails and double bubble-roof
panel look very much like a concept vehicle.
Also, the design of the front and rear gives you
a feeling of security.

speaker: Shiro Nakamura
en:
�sseq scmd="GTCafe_Conv_Standard01">At the risk of sounding crass by compliment our own designs...

...I always felt that the GT-R in the Super GT Series was
"oh so cool" when watching it in races. 
The racecar is modified by NISMO every year...

...and the original image of the GT-R is carefully retained in 
the grille and the shape of the lights.

When watching a race, it's important to be able to 
recognize a car when seeing it from a distance. 
For that to happen, the front and rear of 
the base production car must be distinctive. 
Also, while race cars may be modified for aerodynamics,

Without a doubt, the Mini is one of the world's
most popular compact cars.
It was introduced in Britain in 1959.

Its outward appearance was left largely unchanged
over the course of its 40-year production history.
In 2001, it was reborn in the form of the next-generation Mini
